messages.Text: user just logged in by mobile OTP, but profile call says ABDM-1094 X-token expired. token is brand new, why?

reply.Text: I'll look up that error code to understand what's happening.

atoms.body:
# ABDM-1094, access to this feature is refused

## In plain words

Your client, or the person's token, is not allowed to do what the call tried. The M1 calls return `ABDM-1094` with HTTP 401 and one of three messages:

- "X-token expired", on child ABHA enrolment. The parent's `X-token` has expired.
- "Invalid Benefit Name", on benefit link and de-link. The `BENEFIT_NAME` header does not name a benefit programme your client can use.
- "Access to this feature is restricted. Please contact NHA to enable it.", on benefit link and de-link. Your client is not enabled for this feature.

## What happens

This code arrives with `code` at the top level beside a `timestamp`, while other M1 errors wrap it in an `error` object. Read the `code` inside `error` when it is present, and fall back to the top level `code`.

## When it goes wrong

Retrying does not help. For "X-token expired", have the parent log in again and send the new `X-token`. For "Invalid Benefit Name", send the benefit name exactly as registered, as in the example `healthid api`. For the restricted message, stop calling the feature until NHA enables it for your client.
atoms.summary: Your client or the person's token is not allowed to do what the call tried, and the message says which of three cases applies.
atoms.title: ABDM-1094, access to this feature is refused

reply.Text:
The error is specific to **child ABHA enrollment** — the parent's `X-token` has expired. That's the documented reason for ABDM-1094 with "X-token expired".

Even though your token is fresh from login, if you're a child ABHA trying to access using a parent's token, the parent's session may have timed out. 

**What to do:**
- **If you're a child:** have the parent re-authenticate and send you their new `X-token`
- **If you're not in a child scenario:** there may be a clock skew issue or the token endpoint itself is rejecting it — check that the system time on both client and gateway are synchronized, and verify the token response includes a valid expiry time

Which scenario applies — are you authenticating as a child ABHA, or are you the primary account holder?
